title: How ork works: guide with diagrams, and an orchestrator-parity gap analysis

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Owner request 2026-10-29: (1) review how ork operates from its documentation and summarize it; (2) write easy-to-follow diagrams and flowcharts of how ork works, its data flow, and how a user sets up and runs waves and other common tasks; (3) check that ork can itself do everything the orchestrating session does today, so the owner can answer questions, set everything up, run, and monitor progress across projects from ork and never need an orchestrator session. This slice produces the guide and the gap analysis; the gaps become new slices that the outer session files from the analysis. No product code.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: No Go tests. Checks by reading: every command, key and file named in the guide exists in the code or docs (cite file:line in the review); every diagram is Mermaid text, ASCII only; the parity table has one row per orchestrator job with ork's status (exists, partial, missing) and evidence.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Docs only. 1. A Haiku (xhigh) subagent reads the docs (PROJECT.md, docs/*.md, README.md, AGENTS.md) and the CLI help text and summarizes how ork operates: what it owns, the daemon and TUI, projects and the registry, runs, relays, roles and the matrix, waves, questions and owner answers, landing, state files, commands and keys. 2. Write docs/guide.md (a walk-through for a new owner: install, ork doctor, add a project, set it up, run one slice, run a wave, answer questions, approve and land, monitor, recover) and docs/diagrams.md (Mermaid diagrams: components and data flow, run state machine, wave lifecycle, relay roles round, setup-to-first-run, daily monitoring), linked from README.md. Short plain sentences, ASCII only, mark anything not built as *proposed* or *candidate*. 3. Write docs/orchestrator-parity.md: list every job the outer orchestrating session does today (preflight and owner interviews, recording decisions, editing specs and the role matrix, choosing the lineup, starting and parallelizing runs, review/UI pass/gate/fix rounds, ledger recording, landing and pushing, filing later notes, monitoring across projects, adj decisions), and for each say whether ork does it (exists with file:line or doc), partly does it, or cannot, plus a proposed slice title and size for each gap. Not a UI slice for the docs, but flag every gap that would be one.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: slicer check; adj lint; Mermaid text reviewed by reading; all paths and commands named in the docs verified against the code.
